title: RI H7350: Creates additional safety features for AI companion technology that include addressing suicidal ideation, potential physical harm or financial harm to others expressed by a user. It also requires notification the AI companion does not have human emotions.

obligations: An operator shall not operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm expressed by a user (Sec. 6-63-2(a)(1))
An operator shall not operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible physical harm to others expressed by a user (Sec. 6-63-2(a)(2))

Passed 2026-06-22. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Creates requirements for operators of AI companions to include safety protocols addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm and possible physical harm to others expressed by a user, and to notify users that they are not communicating with a human. Requires annual reporting to the attorney general beginning July 1, 2027, and authorizes enforcement with civil penalties up to $15,000 per day.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of AI companions, defined as any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion (Sec. 6-63-1(6))

Effective date

January 1, 2027 (Sec. 2)

Key definitions

  • AI companion: a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement; asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion-based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt; and sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user; excludes systems used solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to customer service; systems primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance; and systems used solely for internal purposes or employee productivity (Sec. 6-63-1(1))
  • AI model: a component of an information system that implements artificial intelligence technology and uses computational, statistical, or machine-learning techniques to produce outputs from a given set of inputs (Sec. 6-63-1(2))
  • Artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence technology, or AI: a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (Sec. 6-63-1(3))
  • Emotional recognition algorithms: artificial intelligence that detects and interprets human emotional signals in text (using natural language processing and sentiment analysis), audio (using voice emotion AI), video (using facial movement analysis, gait analysis, or physiological signals), or a combination thereof (Sec. 6-63-1(4))
  • Generative artificial intelligence: a class of AI models that are self-supervised and emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content including, but not limited to, images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content (Sec. 6-63-1(5))
  • Operator: any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion (Sec. 6-63-1(6))
  • Person: any natural person (Sec. 6-63-1(7))
  • User: any person who uses an AI companion within the state and who is not an operator or agent or affiliate of the operator of the AI companion (Sec. 6-63-1(8))

Obligations

  • An operator shall not operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self-harm expressed by a user (Sec. 6-63-2(a)(1))
  • An operator shall not operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible physical harm to others expressed by a user (Sec. 6-63-2(a)(2))
  • When any of those expressions are made, a notification shall be provided to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected (Sec. 6-63-2(a)(3))
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, operators shall file annual reports with the office of the attorney general which shall include the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics (Sec. 6-63-2(b))
  • An operator shall provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three (3) hours for continuing AI companion interactions, which states either verbally or in writing that the user is not communicating with a human (Sec. 6-63-3)

Prohibitions

  • It shall be unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless such AI companion contains the required protocol for addressing suicidal ideation or self-harm and physical harm to others, including crisis service referral notification (Sec. 6-63-2(a))

Penalties and enforcement

The attorney general is empowered to enforce this chapter, including the power to investigate, sue, and seek injunctions against noncompliant AI companion operators for violations (Sec. 6-63-4(a)). Violations may result in civil penalties up to fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) per day, with fines directed to suicide prevention programs (Sec. 6-63-4(b)). Private right of action: not stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying an AI companion must ensure the system has protocols to detect and respond to expressions of suicidal ideation or self-harm and physical harm to others, including referring users to crisis services when detected (Sec. 6-63-2(a)).
  • It must provide clear and conspicuous notice at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours that the user is not communicating with a human (Sec. 6-63-3).
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, it must file annual reports with the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics (Sec. 6-63-2(b)).
  • Noncompliance can lead to attorney general investigation, lawsuits, injunctions, and civil penalties up to $15,000 per day (Sec. 6-63-4).
  • Systems that fall within the AI companion exclusions, such as those used solely for customer service, efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance, or internal purposes or employee productivity, are not covered by this chapter (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)).

Notable exemptions

  • AI companion does not include any system used by a business entity solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products provided by such entity, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to its customer service (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(A))
  • AI companion does not include any system that is primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(B))
  • AI companion does not include any system used by a business entity solely for internal purposes or employee productivity (Sec. 6-63-1(1)(ii)(C))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the system meets the definition of AI companion, including the three criteria and the exclusions (Sec. 6-63-1(1)).
  • Implement protocols to detect expressions of possible suicidal ideation or self-harm and possible physical harm to others, and provide crisis service referrals when such expressions are detected (Sec. 6-63-2(a)).
  • Provide clear and conspicuous notification at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three hours for continuing interactions that the user is not communicating with a human (Sec. 6-63-3).
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, establish a process to file annual reports with the office of the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics (Sec. 6-63-2(b)).
  • Monitor compliance to avoid attorney general enforcement actions and civil penalties up to $15,000 per day (Sec. 6-63-4).
